clue.text: No one turned up to support investigation under discussion

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: an inquest is an official investigation, typically into a death

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Nobody appeared to back an inquiry that is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NO + I to give ION, which goes under INQUEST in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in question is being debated or considered, not yet settled.

clue.text: Males conceal a low average

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside oneself, so the word for males wraps round the next piece

parts.note: men are males

explanation.surface: Men are hiding a poor batting or exam average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is another sense of the answer (mean, base), backing up the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Long to arrive in an undisputed border city? Hardly

indicators.note: one piece arriving in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A question about yearning to reach a frontier town no one argues over.
explanation.walkthrough: AACHEN, in Germany at the Belgian and Dutch borders, was fought over for centuries (also called Aix-la-Chapelle), so 'undisputed' is ironic, as 'Hardly' admits.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city lies on the meeting point of three national borders and changed hands repeatedly.

clue.text: Live! Dame Edna's pulling power!

parts.note: L marks the live terminal on an electrical plug
Dame Edna's surname is Everage, the comic character created by the Australian Barry Humphries

explanation.surface: A poster bill for a live show starring Dame Edna, trumpeting her drawing power.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edna Everage was the stage persona of comedian Barry Humphries, famous in Britain for TV and theatre shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the mechanical advantage of a lever, and figuratively influence.

clue.text: "It's standing behind you!" yelled by Sherpa?

indicators.note: the second piece comes after, so in a down entry below, the first

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means upright, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: the word it, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: A pantomime-style warning shouted by a Himalayan guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the pantomime cry 'It's behind you!'; 'standing' turns IT into TI below YE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sherpa might cry out on seeing the abominable snowman of Himalayan legend.

clue.text: VW model abandoned by AA's said to attract attention

indicators.note: the car is left without the named letters, which take themselves off

parts.note: the Passat is a Volkswagen car
the letters AA, the 's a link

explanation.surface: A broken-down Volkswagen left by the motoring rescue service, the AA (Automobile Association).
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered hiss used to catch someone's notice quietly.

clue.text: Minister back in dodgy sinecure had people performing below par

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged
back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman holding a cushy, shady post employed slackers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sinecure is a paid post needing little work; 'dodgy' looks like a comment on it but signals the rearrangement, and 'back' turns the minister round.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who do less well than expected are failing to reach their potential.

clue.text: Very occasionally pursues pawn in game

indicators.note: pursues means comes after, so this piece follows the first

parts.note: to hock something is to pawn it

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, here every other one, are taken

explanation.surface: A chess note: a piece rarely chases a pawn during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks the second and fourth letters of 'Very', E and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck.

clue.text: Put out question in French to children

parts.note: the French word for in is en

explanation.surface: A teacher puts a question in French to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To quench a fire is to extinguish it.

clue.text: Drug dealer Mitchell's carelessly dropped a couple of lines

indicators.note: carelessly means the remaining letters are jumbled
the name loses the named letters

parts.note: the name Mitchell with its s
L is short for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: A pusher named Mitchell slipped up and lost some lines of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes LL from MITCHELLS, leaving MITCHES, which 'carelessly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist legitimately dispenses medicines, playfully called drugs.

clue.text: Case not closed? On the contrary, it's in the bag

indicators.note: on the contrary signals turning the letters the other way round
a word not closed is missing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective case left open, though the deal is in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not closed' cuts the last letter from CASE, and 'On the contrary' reverses CAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sac is a pouch-like structure in a plant or animal.

clue.text: Gag lines upset church

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Gagging rules have angered the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to stop them speaking, enforcing quiet.

clue.text: Slip stewing apples, having dropped bit of peel

indicators.note: stewing means cooking down, so the letters are mixed up
having dropped means the fruit's name has let fall one of its letters, which is removed
a bit of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Cooking apples, a cook peels them and drops a sliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes P from 'peel'; 'having dropped' removes one P from APPLES, and 'stewing' rearranges APLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small error or momentary failure.

clue.text: Tribesman's apparently a revolutionary

parts.note: ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparent or apparently
taken as written
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A tribal warrior who seems to be a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Tribesman' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: A girl briefly tours capital of Tunisia and mountains nearby

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a quick trip round Tunisia's capital and the nearby range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas range runs across North Africa, close to Tunisia.

clue.text: Shrill soprano emphasising ritual?

parts.note: a shrill sound is high-pitched
Charlotte Church is a Welsh soprano who became famous as a child singer

explanation.surface: A piercing singer who goes in for ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte Church was a hugely popular British classical-crossover singer around 2000; the '?' flags that the definition describes a churchmanship rather than defining it outright.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Catholic wing of Anglicanism stresses sacraments, vestments and ceremonial worship.

clue.text: Can I insert refurbished amp in percussion?

indicators.note: the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: a tin is a can
taken as written

indicators.note: refurbished means done up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A roadie asks whether to fit a repaired amplifier in the drum section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening a question; it is the noun meaning a tin container. 'refurbished' rearranges the amp's letters and 'insert' places them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are the kettledrums of an orchestra.

clue.text: Drugs agent is going to and fro getting plants

parts.note: narc is US slang for a narcotics officer
taken as written

indicators.note: going to and fro means the word appears forwards then backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An undercover narcotics officer shuttles about obtaining cannabis plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodils and related spring-flowering bulbs.

clue.text: Change position, altering ground after losing time

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so these letters are rearranged
the word loses a letter before the rearranging

explanation.surface: A footballer changes position, rearranging the pitch after wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing' takes T out of ALTERING, leaving ALERING, which 'ground' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to move into a new arrangement or alignment.

clue.text: Simonumentumrequiris, circumspice — this band's motto

parts.note: Wren's Latin epitaph, 'if you seek a monument, look around', tells the solver to look round the grid's edge, where the Old French motto of an English chivalric order is spelt out; that order is named after a band worn on the leg

explanation.walkthrough: The perimeter letters spell HONI SOIT QUI MAL Y PENSE, motto of the Order of the Garter, Britain's senior order of knighthood; 'band' puns on the garter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter is an elastic band worn round the leg, and gives its name to the order whose motto rings the grid.

clue.text: Ready to drive off, emerges from A19 avoiding a learner

indicators.note: the result comes out of the jumbled letters of what remains
avoiding means leaving out the named letters

parts.note: the letter A plus the answer to 19 Across
A as written plus L, the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A motorist is set to leave, turning off the A19 road to avoid a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: A19 reads as A plus 19 Across; 'avoiding' removes A and L to leave REAIGN, which 'emerges from' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A car in gear is engaged and ready to move.

clue.text: Move on, say, northwards, bypassing east

indicators.note: bypassing means passing by, so the letter is placed alongside
in a down entry, northwards means read upwards

parts.note: eg means for example, say
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Directions to a driver heading north on a bypass round the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses EG to GE, and E is added below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is a command to a horse to go on or speed up.

clue.text: Having communication problem, a computer has one installed

parts.note: PC is a personal computer
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

clue.text: Ambassador meets a fellow face to face

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
taken as written
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A diplomat confronts a college fellow in person.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on encounter is direct, confronting someone directly.

clue.text: Intermediary put money on Chocolate Bar coming in third

parts.note: to bet is to put money on something
Twix is a brand of chocolate bar

explanation.surface: A punter backs a chocolate bar that finishes third in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Twix is a chocolate biscuit bar made by Mars, sold in Britain and elsewhere.

clue.text: Brilliant inventor read out introductions for writer

clue.text: Dresses oddly, though succeeded

indicators.note: oddly means the first, third and fifth letters are taken

parts.note: S is short for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: She dresses strangely, but still succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To tog someone up is to clothe them in fine garments.

clue.text: Dislike irritable musician who's not in charge

the word loses the named letters

explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or ill will.

clue.text: Reinforcements carry much more than dope

indicators.note: the long word carries the short one within its letters

clue.text: Unions here in Bognor attempt to cool off inside?

a try is an attempt
taken as written
to ice is to cool
